claimed_purpose.text: ReMe is a file-native memory system with a defined memory lifecycle spanning ingestion through proactive topics.
ReMe is described as a personal knowledge base that grows after every conversation.
ReMe is described as a memory toolkit that can support companion-style systems
AutoMemoryStep records conversation facts into a daily note via an agent

mechanisms.text: ReMe uses a BM25 keyword index for search, fed by chunks emitted from MarkdownFileChunker. Frontmatter fields (name, description, tags) are parsed into metadata but not emitted as searchable text, so they are invisible to BM25 search.
Workspace root is configurable, and per-item workspaces can be reused (eval_only mode re-queries pre-built memory without re-ingesting), indicating the store persists independently of the query step.
ReMe supports an auto_dream feature that can be triggered when sessions cross a configured hour, suggesting a background summarization or consolidation process distinct from raw session ingestion.
auto_memory distills useful conversation facts from conversation while preserving a filtered conversation source record (JSONL log) separately from curated daily memory cards
proactive_read reads interest topics produced by a separate proactive refresh flow; host agent decides whether to act — retrieve policy is adaptive, not always-on injection
The benchmark preset uses a modified auto-memory prompt with auto_dream disabled, indicating a prompt-scaffold layer that instructs the model how to use retrieved memory.
Retrieve policy uses BM25 plus optional embeddings fused via reciprocal rank fusion, returning matching chunks with line ranges and bounded wikilink neighbors
The edit command auto-appends the .md suffix via gate_md(), but stat, frontmatter_read, and frontmatter_update do not, causing inconsistent path resolution.
Raw CC entries are appended into ReMe's own CC SessionStore; deduplication by record uuid identifies only the increment (new turns) since the last stop.
A graph-chunk consistency repair step exists but only detects graph-vs-store id mismatches; it cannot detect stale chunks that are consistently wrong.
Rename/retarget on update: if the Agent supplies a better frontmatter name on update, the system can rename the note and retarget inbound wikilinks.
Session lifecycle hooks record durable session knowledge automatically without blocking agent shutdown, indicating a write path tied to session end.
ReMe uses a dedicated service LLM for memory extraction and retrieval, separate from the agent LLM used for task reasoning.
An endpoint /add_task_memory is expected to exist on the HTTP backend to ingest task memories during pool initialization.
ReMe exposes an HTTP service entrypoint, with two copies suggesting an in-progress v3→v4 migration (reme/ and reme4/)
Procedure deduplication and recall is scoped to current project plus global procedures, excluding other projects
ReMe surfaces a 'Memory as File' mechanism, indicating memory is persisted as files on the local filesystem.
Store is file-native in a user-owned local workspace; index is rebuildable and separate from source files
ReMe uses a file-native workspace model with explicit source-of-truth boundaries and generated indexes.
ReMe includes an Auto Memory feature, suggesting automated extraction or writing to the memory store.
Session message log path is <session_dir>/dialog/<session_id>.jsonl — isolation is per session_id
v0.3 lacked BM25 keyword search and RRF fusion; v0.4 introduces these alongside vector search
Multiple agents can share one workspace; memory isolation is per workspace, not per agent
A ReMe.forget() method exists and is described as a cleanup path that could be extended
Embeddings are disabled by default; enabling them requires explicit config changes
In v0.4 the file-native approach became core and vector retrieval was made opt-in
Wiki namespace remains global and is not subdivided by project
